title: Smart Parking Assistant
tagline: Detect available parking spots and alert drivers with LEDs and a buzzer.
overview: Build a miniature smart parking system that uses ultrasonic sensors to detect whether a parking bay is occupied. An LED matrix (green/red LEDs) shows availability, and a buzzer alerts when the last slot fills. Ideal for learning distance sensing and conditional logic.
realWorldProblem: Urban parking congestion wastes fuel and time. Smart parking systems reduce this by directing drivers to open bays instantly.
assemblySteps: Place the breadboard on a flat surface.
Insert both HC-SR04 sensors at opposite ends of the breadboard.
Connect each sensor: VCC→5V, GND→GND, TRIG and ECHO to assigned Arduino digital pins.
Insert four LEDs (green and red pairs) with 220Ω resistors in series.
Connect all LED cathodes to GND rail.
Insert the active buzzer with + to D10 and − to GND.
Double-check all VCC and GND connections before powering on.
Upload the sketch and open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud to verify distances.
uploadInstructions: 1. Open Arduino IDE. 2. Paste the sketch. 3. Select Tools > Board > Arduino UNO. 4. Select the correct COM port. 5. Click Upload (→). 6. Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud.
expectedBehavior: Green LEDs light when a bay is free; red LEDs light when occupied. The buzzer activates when both bays are occupied. Serial Monitor shows real-time distances.

troubleshooting.fix: Check TRIG/ECHO wiring. Ensure pulseIn timeout is long enough (30000 µs).

troubleshooting.problem: LED stays on all the time
troubleshooting.fix: Check resistor is in series, not in parallel. Verify pin assignments match the sketch.
Confirm it is an active buzzer. Check polarity.

safetyNotes: Keep sensor voltage at 5V. Do not short-circuit the buzzer. Ensure resistors are fitted before LEDs.

title: Soil Moisture Monitoring System
tagline: Monitor plant soil moisture and trigger an LED/buzzer alert when watering is needed.
overview: A soil moisture sensor reads analog values from the soil. When moisture falls below a threshold the Arduino activates a red LED and buzzer to prompt watering. A green LED confirms adequate moisture. Ideal first project for agricultural IoT.
realWorldProblem: Over-watering and under-watering are the leading causes of crop loss for small farmers. Automated soil monitoring conserves water and improves yield.
assemblySteps: Insert the soil moisture sensor probe into the breadboard.
Connect VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and AOUT to A0.
Insert red LED with 220Ω resistor to D8.
Insert green LED with 220Ω resistor to D9.
Connect buzzer + to D10 and − to GND.
Upload the sketch and insert the probe into dry soil.
Gradually add water and observe the threshold change in Serial Monitor.
uploadInstructions: 1. Open Arduino IDE. 2. Paste the sketch. 3. Select Board > Arduino UNO. 4. Upload. 5. Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud to read moisture values.
expectedBehavior: Green LED on when soil has adequate moisture. Red LED and buzzer pulse when soil is dry. Adjust DRY_THRESHOLD constant to calibrate for your soil type.

troubleshooting.fix: Check AOUT is connected to A0, not a digital pin. Ensure sensor is properly inserted in soil.
Adjust DRY_THRESHOLD — dry soil typically reads 600–900 on a 5V Arduino.

safetyNotes: Do not submerge the sensor module PCB in water — only the stainless steel probes. Dry the probes after use to extend life.

title: Water Tank Level Alert
tagline: Monitor water tank levels with ultrasonic sensing and LED indicators.
overview: An HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor mounted inside a water tank measures the distance to the water surface, allowing the Arduino to calculate fill percentage. Three LEDs (green/yellow/red) and a buzzer indicate full, half, and low levels.
realWorldProblem: Overflowing tanks waste water and cause structural damage. Manual monitoring is impractical for rooftop tanks. An automated alert system conserves water and prevents overflow.
assemblySteps: Mount sensor facing downward at the top inside of a container (representing the tank).
Measure the total tank height in cm — update TANK_HEIGHT in the sketch.
Wire sensor VCC/GND/TRIG/ECHO as in the wiring table.
Insert LEDs with resistors and buzzer as specified.
Upload sketch and pour water to test each threshold.
Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud to read raw distance and fill percentage.
uploadInstructions: Upload via Arduino IDE. Set TANK_HEIGHT to your container's inner height in cm. Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud.
expectedBehavior: Green LED for > 66% full. Yellow LED for 33–66%. Red LED and buzzer for < 33%. Buzzer triggers as low-level alert below 15%.

troubleshooting.fix: Check TRIG/ECHO pins. Sensor must face straight down and be within 4m range.
Update TANK_HEIGHT to accurately reflect your container's inner height.

safetyNotes: Keep the sensor PCB clear of water contact. Only the sound-emitting face should be near moisture. Use waterproof JST connectors for permanent installations.

title: Temperature and Humidity Monitor
tagline: Display real-time temperature and humidity on an LCD or Serial Monitor.
overview: A DHT11 sensor reads ambient temperature and humidity, displaying values on a 16×2 I2C LCD. A warning LED activates at high temperatures. Great for greenhouse monitoring, weather stations, or server room alerts.
realWorldProblem: Unmonitored temperature in server rooms, greenhouses, and storage facilities causes equipment failure and crop loss. A low-cost sensor provides early warning.
assemblySteps: Insert DHT11 module into breadboard. Connect VCC, GND, DATA.
Connect I2C LCD: SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC to 5V, GND to GND.
Insert red LED with 220Ω resistor to D8.
Install DHT library: Sketch > Include Library > Manage Libraries > search 'DHT sensor library' by Adafruit > Install.
Install LiquidCrystal_I2C library: search 'LiquidCrystal I2C' by Frank de Brabander > Install.
Upload the sketch and observe values on the LCD.
uploadInstructions: Install both libraries from Library Manager. Upload the sketch. If the LCD shows nothing, run an I2C scanner sketch to find the correct address (0x27 or 0x3F).
expectedBehavior: LCD shows live temperature in °C and humidity in %. Red LED activates above 35°C threshold. Values update every 2 seconds.

troubleshooting.fix: Adjust the contrast potentiometer on the I2C backpack. Verify I2C address — run I2C scanner sketch.
Ensure DATA pin wiring is correct. Add a 10kΩ pull-up resistor between DATA and VCC if using bare DHT11 (not module).

safetyNotes: DHT11 operates at 3.3–5V. Do not expose to condensing humidity above 95%.

title: Touchless Smart Dustbin
tagline: Open a dustbin lid automatically when a hand is detected nearby.
overview: A servo motor opens a dustbin lid when an HC-SR04 detects a hand within 15 cm. The lid closes automatically after 3 seconds. Promotes hygiene by eliminating touch contact with waste bins.
realWorldProblem: Touching waste bin lids is a major vector for germ spread in homes, hospitals, and public spaces. A touchless mechanism eliminates this contact.
assemblySteps: Attach the servo to the bin lid with a small bracket or hot glue.
Position the HC-SR04 sensor on the front face of the bin pointing outward.
Wire both components as per the wiring table.
Upload the sketch and test with hand detection.
Adjust OPEN_DISTANCE and LID_DELAY constants as needed.
Servo angle (0°=closed, 90°=open) can be calibrated in the sketch.
uploadInstructions: The Servo library is built into Arduino IDE. Upload the sketch directly. Calibrate servo angles 0 and 90 to fit your lid geometry.
expectedBehavior: Lid opens to 90° when hand detected within 15 cm. Closes after 3 seconds. Serial Monitor shows real-time distance readings.

troubleshooting.fix: Add a 100µF capacitor across servo VCC and GND. Use an external 5V supply for the servo if the Arduino power is insufficient.
Adjust delay between servo angle increments for smooth movement.

safetyNotes: SG90 servo draws up to 250mA. Ensure the Arduino USB power supply can handle the load; use a 1A+ adapter.

title: Obstacle Detection Alert
tagline: Detect objects ahead and warn with a buzzer — foundation for robot collision avoidance.
overview: Uses an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor to detect objects within a set range and activates a buzzer and red LED alert. The buzzer beeps faster as the object gets closer. This is the foundational module for robot obstacle avoidance.
realWorldProblem: Collision avoidance is critical for autonomous vehicles, assistive robots for the visually impaired, and warehouse automation.
assemblySteps: Connect HC-SR04 as per wiring table.
Connect buzzer + to D7 and − to GND.
Connect red LED anode via 220Ω resistor to D8 and cathode to GND.
Upload the sketch.
Hold your hand in front of the sensor at varying distances to test.
uploadInstructions: No libraries needed. Upload directly. Adjust ALERT_DIST constant for your use case.
expectedBehavior: Red LED lights and buzzer beeps when obstacle within 30 cm. Beep frequency increases as distance decreases. Serial Monitor shows distance readings.

troubleshooting.fix: Object may be permanently in range. Increase ALERT_DIST or check for reflective surfaces near the sensor.

safetyNotes: HC-SR04 operates at 5V. Do not exceed 15mA through the LED — ensure resistor is fitted.

title: Smart Plant Care Monitor
tagline: Monitor soil moisture, light, and temperature to keep your plant healthy.
overview: Combines a soil moisture sensor, LDR (light sensor), and DHT11 temperature sensor to give a complete plant health dashboard on the Serial Monitor. LED indicators show which condition needs attention. Ideal for urban gardening.
realWorldProblem: Urban dwellers often struggle to keep plants alive due to inconsistent care. An automated care monitor reminds users when to water, provides more light, or adjust temperature.
assemblySteps: Insert soil moisture sensor probes and connect to A0.
Build LDR voltage divider: LDR from 5V to A1 node, 10kΩ from A1 node to GND.
Connect DHT11 DATA to D2.
Insert three LEDs with 220Ω resistors to D5, D6, D7.
Install DHT library from Arduino Library Manager.
Upload the sketch.
Place probes in soil, LDR facing light source, and observe LED indicators.
uploadInstructions: Install DHT library. Upload sketch. Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud for all readings.
expectedBehavior: Red LED = needs water. Blue LED = needs more light. Yellow LED = temperature too high. All LEDs off = plant is healthy.

troubleshooting.fix: Check DATA wiring and library installation.
Adjust DARK_THRESHOLD — a bright indoor environment reads 600–900; DARK_THRESHOLD of 300 may be too low.

safetyNotes: Do not submerge the sensor module PCB. Keep electrical connections away from the soil and water.

title: Water Usage Monitoring Prototype
tagline: Measure simulated water flow and display cumulative usage to promote conservation.
overview: A YF-S201 water flow sensor sends pulses proportional to flow rate. The Arduino counts pulses to calculate litres consumed and displays the total on a 16×2 I2C LCD. A threshold alert triggers a buzzer when a daily limit is exceeded.
realWorldProblem: Households in water-scarce regions often have no visibility into daily water consumption. Simple metering raises awareness and drives conservation behaviour.
assemblySteps: Connect YF-S201 sensor to the water pipe using fittings (for prototype, simulate pulses by briefly connecting D2 to 5V through 1kΩ resistor).
Wire I2C LCD as specified.
Connect buzzer to D8.
Install LiquidCrystal_I2C library.
Upload the sketch.
Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud to verify pulse counts.
uploadInstructions: Install LiquidCrystal_I2C. For prototype testing without plumbing, briefly pulse D2 with a wire connected to 5V through a 1kΩ resistor. Upload the sketch and observe counts.
expectedBehavior: LCD shows current flow rate in L/min and cumulative total. Buzzer activates when total exceeds DAILY_LIMIT_L (50L default). Reset Arduino to clear total.

troubleshooting.fix: Ensure D2 is used (interrupt pin on UNO). Check FALLING/RISING edge for your sensor.
Run an I2C scanner to find the correct address (0x27 or 0x3F).

safetyNotes: YF-S201 is rated for water only — not for chemicals. Ensure all electrical connections are kept away from water flow path. Use waterproof connectors for permanent installation.
